# Rachel Lynde

## Overview

- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v1 c1 P0](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0000)</sub>
- **Status:** Widowed  <sub>[v3 c37 P0](../source/v03-c37.md#nw-v03-c37-p0000)</sub>
- **Role:** Housewife  <sub>[v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001)</sub>

## Appearance

Mrs. Rachel Lynde is a fat, stout woman who waddles when she walks, though she remains neat and matronly in her attire. As she ages, she complains of the physical burden of her weight, yet maintains a bustling, energetic presence.

_Sources: [v1 c9 P31](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0031), [v1 c29 P30](../source/v01-c29.md#nw-v01-c29-p0030), [v2 c14 P0](../source/v02-c14.md#nw-v02-c14-p0000), [v3 c1 P8](../source/v03-c01.md#nw-v03-c01-p0008)_

## Personality

Mrs. Rachel Lynde is an outspoken, capable, and formidable woman who prides herself on speaking her mind without fear or favor. Highly industrious and managing, she involves herself deeply in both her own affairs and those of her neighbors. Though she can be blunt, opinionated, and sharp-tongued, she possesses a warm, kind heart and is always among the first to offer practical help to those in need. She holds strong religious and political convictions, remaining a devout Presbyterian and an ardent Liberal.

_Sources: [v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001), [v1 c1 P24](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0024), [v1 c9 P14](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0014), [v1 c18 P1](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0001), [v2 c7 P3](../source/v02-c07.md#nw-v02-c07-p0003), [v2 c7 P31](../source/v02-c07.md#nw-v02-c07-p0031), [v2 c14 P10](../source/v02-c14.md#nw-v02-c14-p0010)_

## History

Mrs. Rachel Lynde lived for over forty-five years in Lynde's Hollow, keeping a vigilant eye on all Avonlea happenings. When Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert decided to adopt a child, she initially strongly disapproved of bringing an orphan into Green Gables. Her first meeting with Anne Shirley resulted in a fierce explosion of temper when Rachel criticized the girl's looks, though she quickly accepted Anne's dramatic apology and grew quite fond of her over time. Following the death of her husband, Thomas Lynde, after a long illness, Rachel was forced to sell her mortgaged farm. Marilla Cuthbert invited her to move to Green Gables, where she set up her own quarters in the north gable. There, she assisted Marilla in managing the household and raising the young twins, Davy and Dora Keith, while Anne attended Redmond College. She continued her active involvement in the church Ladies' Aid Society and local affairs, remaining an indispensable pillar of the Avonlea community.

_Sources: [v1 c1 P0](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0000), [v1 c1 P25](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0025), [v1 c9 P14](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0014), [v1 c9 P16](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0016), [v1 c10 P30](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0030), [v1 c10 P38](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0038), [v2 c26 P0](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0000), [v2 c26 P15](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0015), [v2 c26 P21](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0021), [v2 c26 P26](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0026), [v3 c1 P7](../source/v03-c01.md#nw-v03-c01-p0007)_

## Background by volume

- Lived in Lynde's Hollow, Avonlea, for most of her married life  <sub>[v1 c1 P0](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0000), [v2 c26 P17](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0017)</sub>

## Quotes

> There are plenty of people, in Avonlea and out of it, who can attend closely to their neighbors’ business by dint of neglecting their own; but Mrs. Rachel Lynde was one of those capable creatures who can manage their own concerns and those of other folks into the bargain.  <sub>[v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001)</sub>

> Blessed are they who expect nothing for they shall not be disappointed.  <sub>[v1 c13 P19](../source/v01-c13.md#nw-v01-c13-p0019)</sub>

> Mark my words, Thomas, Marilla Cuthbert 'll live to rue the step she’s took.  <sub>[v1 c30 P43](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0043)</sub>

> Avonlea must keep up with the procession, that’s what.  <sub>[v4 c1 P12](../source/v04-c01.md#nw-v04-c01-p0012)</sub>

> I’m not going to argue with you, Anne. I am not a B.A. What time of the day is the ceremony to be?  <sub>[v4 c3 P20](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0020)</sub>
